meta.note: Deterministic rules behind the generated examples. Edit them freely. No model is called.

distance.rule: Two parts count as distant when they sit in different domains and run in different places. This is a sorting rule, not a measure of how good a pairing is.

fit.direct: Same shape: what the first gives is what the second takes.
fit.adapter: Different shapes, and the rule table names a transformation.
fit.none: No transformation in the rule table. That may be a dead end, or a bridge nobody has named.

playful.title: Slow down {give}
playful.outcome: {B} receives {give} only once a week. Treat it as an event rather than a feed.
playful.test: Pick this week's one by hand and notice what you left out.
playful.success: The one you chose tells you something the rest would have hidden.

playful.title: Let {B} misread {give} on purpose
playful.outcome: Hand {B} {give} in the wrong spirit and keep the most interesting failure.
playful.test: Imagine three wrong readings on paper before touching any tool.
playful.success: One misreading gives you an idea you would not have had.

playful.title: Make {give} something you can hold
playful.outcome: Whatever {B} does with {give} has to end as an object or a place in the room.
playful.test: Sketch what would sit on the desk.
playful.success: Someone else can tell what it means without an explanation.

questions.title: What does {give} know that {B} has never been shown?
questions.outcome: A research direction: list what {A} sees that {B} has no way of seeing.

questions.title: Which decision would change if {B} received {give} every week?
questions.outcome: Name the decision first. If none changes, this bridge may not matter.

questions.title: What would {B} get wrong if {give} were all it knew?
questions.outcome: Use the error to find what is missing from {A}.

exercises.name: Two distant parts
exercises.ask: Connect a device or data source with a tool from another domain.

exercises.name: Missing middle
exercises.ask: These shapes do not match. Name the transformation that would make them fit.

exercises.name: Add one thing
exercises.ask: Add a third part that changes the result substantially, not one that just extends it.

exercises.name: Reverse the arrow
exercises.ask: Does the outcome change when the information flows the other way?

exercises.name: Swap a resource
exercises.ask: Substitute a free or local part and look at what you gain and lose.

exercises.name: A small purchase
exercises.ask: Which blocked bridges open at a stated cost, and which were not blocked by money at all?

exercises.name: Transfer
exercises.ask: A fresh pair and no examples. Build the bridge unaided, then save it before you compare.

exercises.name: Shortest route
exercises.ask: Take parts away until the idea breaks. The last part you could not remove is the one that matters.

exercises.name: The long way round
exercises.ask: Reach the same end in at least three hops. What does each extra stop do that a direct line cannot?

exercises.name: Two into one
exercises.ask: Bring two unrelated sources into one part. What can they show together that neither shows alone?

exercises.name: One into two
exercises.ask: Send one thing to two places. What do you learn from the difference between what comes out?

exercises.name: Close the loop
exercises.ask: Let what comes out change what goes in next time. What stops it running away?

shapes.name: One hop
shapes.invite: Could this work with nothing in between?

shapes.name: Chain
shapes.invite: What would a stop along the way do to the result?

shapes.name: Two into one
shapes.invite: What could two sources show that neither shows alone?

shapes.name: One into two
shapes.invite: What would you learn by sending the same thing to two places?

shapes.name: Loop
shapes.invite: What if the end changed the beginning next time?
